description: This file defines a Python module for Spark's streaming query listener interface, including classes for event handling, progress tracking, and Java-Python integration.

classes.name: StreamingQueryListener
classes.description: Interface for listening to streaming query events, with methods for query start, progress, idle, and termination.

classes.name: JStreamingQueryListener
classes.description: Java interface implementation for Python StreamingQueryListener via Py4J.

classes.name: QueryStartedEvent
classes.description: Represents the start event of a streaming query, including IDs, timestamp, and job tags.

classes.name: QueryProgressEvent
classes.description: Represents progress updates of a streaming query, including detailed progress info.

classes.name: QueryIdleEvent
classes.description: Represents an event when a query is idle and waiting for data.

classes.name: QueryTerminatedEvent
classes.description: Represents the termination event of a query, with optional exception info.

classes.name: StreamingQueryProgress
classes.description: Tracks detailed progress of a streaming query, subclass of dict with progress metrics.

classes.name: StateOperatorProgress
classes.description: Tracks progress of stateful operators within a query.

classes.name: SourceProgress
classes.description: Tracks progress of data sources in streaming queries.

classes.name: SinkProgress
classes.description: Tracks progress of data sinks in streaming queries.

methods.name: _set_spark_session
methods.description: Associates a SparkSession with the listener.

methods.name: onQueryStarted
methods.description: Abstract method called when a query starts.

methods.name: onQueryProgress
methods.description: Abstract method called on query progress updates.

methods.name: onQueryIdle
methods.description: Method called when query is idle; default implementation does nothing.

methods.name: onQueryTerminated
methods.description: Abstract method called when a query terminates.

methods.name: _jlistener
methods.description: Returns the Java-side listener object, creating it if necessary.

methods.name: fromJObject
methods.description: Creates event objects from Java objects.

methods.name: fromJson
methods.description: Creates event objects from JSON dictionaries.
